chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from Abu Shaybah al-Zuhri, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
Woe be to the community that does not worship Allah through enjoining good and forbidding evil.

key_terms.وَيْلٌ: Woe or destruction (a warning of punishment)
key_terms.يُدِينُونَ اللَّهَ: They worship/serve Allah (literally: they make their religion for Allah)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to worship Allah through enjoining good and forbidding evil?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), 'enjoining good and forbidding evil' is elevated from a mere social duty to the very essence of 'al-din' (religion), indicating that communal religious identity is contingent upon active moral enforcement. This aligns with the Shia scholarly view that this principle is a collective obligation (fard kifayah) necessary to preserve the integrity of the Ummah. The warning of 'wail' (woe) underscores the spiritual peril of neglecting this pillar, which serves as the mechanism for societal reform and divine justice.
